next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — GoVoteWV

glance_notes.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — GoVoteWV
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: West Virginia's voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 13. West Virginia does not provide general Election Day voter registration.

glance_notes.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — GoVoteWV
glance_notes.text: Early Voting October 21–31: Any registered West Virginia voter may vote early in person without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting runs from October 21 through October 31, including Saturdays during the early-voting period.

glance_notes.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — Polling Place Lookup
glance_notes.text: Election Day Polls 6:30 a.m.–7:30 p.m.: West Virginia polling places are open from 6:30 a.m. until 7:30 p.m. on Election Day. Voters should use the Secretary of State's polling-place lookup to confirm their assigned location.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible West Virginia residents may register online, by mail or in person. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, reside in West Virginia and the county where the person registers, and be at least 18 years old by the General Election. A person who is 17 years old and will turn 18 by the next General Election may register and may participate in the preceding Primary Election. A person serving a sentence, including probation or parole, for a felony, treason or election bribery is not eligible to register until the sentence is completed. A person who has been judicially declared mentally incompetent is not eligible while that disqualification remains in effect.
register.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: West Virginia's felony rule differs from states that restore voting rights immediately after release from incarceration. Current state law generally requires completion of the sentence, including probation or parole. Reverify this language against current Secretary of State guidance and W. Va. Code § 3-2-2 if the statute changes.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the West Virginia Secretary of State's Search My Registration / Polling Place tool to check voter registration status, political party, political districts and assigned polling place. The information reflects the most recent county entry and is updated nightly. Voters with questions or recent changes should contact their County Clerk.
check_registration.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — Search My Registration / Polling Place
check_registration.internal_note: The official lookup directly provides registration status, party, political districts and polling place. The site warns that same-day record activity does not appear until the following day because data is updated nightly.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, West Virginia's voter registration deadline is Tuesday, October 13. A new registration or applicable registration update must meet the state's deadline requirements to take effect for the General Election. West Virginia does not offer general same-day voter registration on Election Day.
deadlines.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — GoVoteWV
deadlines.internal_note: West Virginia's registration cutoff is 21 days before an election. For November 3, 2026, that date is October 13. Do not imply that a generally unregistered voter may simply register at the polls on Election Day. Limited statutory procedures exist for specific registration circumstances, but they are not general same-day registration.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use the West Virginia Secretary of State's polling-place lookup to find your assigned Election Day polling location. West Virginia voters generally vote at the polling place assigned to their precinct. Polling locations may change in emergency situations, so voters should check their location shortly before Election Day or contact their County Clerk if they have questions.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your assigned polling place through GoVoteWV
polling_place.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — Polling Place Lookup
polling_place.internal_note: The official lookup expressly tells voters to vote at their assigned polling location and warns that locations may change during emergencies.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: West Virginia's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 6:30 a.m. until 7:30 p.m. Voters voting in person generally must present an approved form of identification unless they qualify for an exception under state law. Voters should go to their assigned polling location and confirm that location before Election Day.
election_day.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — 2026 Elections Calendar
election_day.internal_note: The official 2026 Elections Calendar expressly identifies November 3 as General Election Day and gives polling hours of 6:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m. W. Va. Code § 3-1-31 independently confirms the same statewide hours.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: West Virginia polling places are open from 6:30 a.m. until 7:30 p.m. on Election Day. Voters should confirm their assigned polling place before voting because locations can change in emergency situations.
polling_hours.internal_note: W. Va. Code § 3-1-31(b) directly establishes 6:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m. for primary, general and special elections.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Any registered West Virginia voter may vote early in person without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting begins Wednesday, October 21 and ends Saturday, October 31. Early voting is conducted during regular business hours on weekdays and from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on Saturdays during the early-voting period. Voters should contact their County Clerk or use official county information to confirm early-voting locations.
early_voting.internal_note: Current W. Va. Code § 3-3-3 establishes early voting from the 13th day before the election through the third day before the election during regular business hours, plus Saturdays from 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. For November 3, 2026, that produces October 21-31. There is no Sunday early voting requirement in this provision.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: West Virginia provides absentee voting by request for voters who meet one of the eligibility categories established by state law. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the regular absentee application period runs from August 11 through October 28, and the County Clerk must receive a regular absentee-by-mail application no later than October 28. A completed absentee ballot may be hand-delivered to the County Clerk's office no later than November 2. A ballot returned by mail generally must be postmarked by Election Day. A ballot with a qualifying Election Day-or-earlier postmark may be accepted through November 9, while an otherwise qualifying ballot received November 4 without a postmark may also be accepted under West Virginia's election calendar.
absentee_mail.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — Absentee Voting Information
absentee_mail.internal_note: West Virginia is not a universal no-excuse mail-voting state. The official 2026 calendar confirms August 11-October 28 as the regular application period, October 28 as the application deadline, November 2 as the hand-delivery deadline, November 4 for otherwise qualifying ballots received without a postmark and November 9 for ballots postmarked by Election Day. The Secretary of State's absentee page states that ordinary domestic mailed ballots must be postmarked by Election Day and received by the start of canvass. Emergency absentee procedures also exist beginning seven days before the election through noon Election Day for qualifying voters.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: West Virginia voters generally must show an approved form of identification when voting in person during early voting or on Election Day. The state's current voter-ID law generally requires a valid, unexpired identifying document that meets statutory requirements. Several exceptions apply, including certain voters accompanied by an adult who has known the voter for at least six months, certain poll workers who have known the voter for at least six months, residents of qualifying state care facilities voting at their precinct, and voters who qualify for specified religious objections. Additional identification requirements apply to some first-time voters.
voter_id.glance_value: Approved ID generally required; statutory exceptions apply
voter_id.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — Voter Identification Information
voter_id.internal_note: The current Secretary of State page says West Virginia voters must show approved photo identification during early voting or Election Day and that identification must be valid and unexpired, but statutory exceptions are important. Do not present the requirement as absolute. First-time voters subject to HAVA may have separate documentation requirements. Absentee-by-mail voters are not generally subject to the ordinary in-person photo-ID requirement, although first-time absentee voters who have not previously satisfied HAVA identification requirements must provide qualifying identification.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: West Virginia provides accessible voting equipment and voter assistance for voters with disabilities. During statewide elections, every polling place has at least one voting machine accessible to voters with disabilities. A voter who needs assistance because of blindness, disability, advanced age or inability to read or write may bring someone to assist or request assistance from two poll workers. If an assigned polling place is inaccessible because of a disability, the voter should contact the County Clerk as soon as possible to arrange voting at another location. Certain voters with physical disabilities may also qualify for electronic absentee voting.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible machine at every statewide-election polling place
accessible_voting.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — Elections FAQs
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly confirms at least one accessible voting machine at every polling place during statewide elections. The site also confirms voter assistance and an alternative-location procedure when a voter's assigned polling place is inaccessible. West Virginia provides an electronic absentee system for eligible voters with physical disabilities.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: West Virginia provides special absentee-voting procedures for eligible members of the uniformed services, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living overseas under UOCAVA. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot and may use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot when applicable. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, military and overseas voters may apply for an absentee ballot from January 1 through October 28. West Virginia permits qualifying UOCAVA voters to receive and return ballots electronically through authorized methods. The state's electronic system allows ballot return by mail, email, fax or the secure online portal.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA/FWAB available; electronic ballot return permitted
military_overseas.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — UOCAVA
military_overseas.internal_note: West Virginia is unusual in expressly allowing UOCAVA voters to return ballots through mail, email, fax or the state's secure OmniBallot portal. The official 2026 calendar lists January 1-October 28 as the military/overseas absentee application period and states that a military or overseas voter who applied absentee for the Primary automatically receives a General Election ballot. Electronically submitted ballots from eligible voters are accepted through close of polls on Election Day.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in West Virginia if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residency requirements. A student should register using the residence the student considers the legal voting residence and may vote in only one jurisdiction in an election. Students who are registered in West Virginia but will be away from their county because of school may qualify for absentee voting under West Virginia's statutory eligibility rules. A person who is 17 years old and will turn 18 by the next General Election may register and vote in the preceding Primary Election.
student_voting.glance_value: Qualifying students away from home may use absentee voting
student_voting.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — Register to Vote
student_voting.internal_note: Do not imply that merely attending a West Virginia college automatically establishes West Virginia voting residency. The absentee-voting rules include voters who are absent from their county for qualifying reasons, including education-related absence under applicable state law. West Virginia also allows a 17-year-old who will be 18 by the General Election to participate in the corresponding Primary.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: West Virginia ballots vary by county, precinct and political district. Voters should use GoVoteWV, their County Clerk and official county election materials to review the ballot that applies to their residence when sample ballots are available. The Secretary of State also publishes statewide candidate information and information about statewide constitutional amendments.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Check GoVoteWV and your County Clerk
sample_ballot.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — GoVoteWV
sample_ballot.internal_note: As of August 30, 2026, GoVoteWV provides the 2026 General Candidate Listing and information about the 2026 Proposed Constitutional Amendment. County and precinct contests vary, so final voter-specific ballot content should be reverified closer to November 3.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: West Virginia Secretary of State, Elections Division, State Capitol Building, Charleston, WV 25305. Phone: 304-558-6000. Toll-free: 866-767-8683. Email: elections@wvsos.gov. For voter-specific registration, polling-place, early-voting or absentee-ballot questions, voters should contact their County Clerk.
contact.source_name: West Virginia Secretary of State — Elections Division
contact.internal_note: Current Secretary of State election pages verify 304-558-6000, toll-free 866-767-8683 and [elections@wvsos.gov](mailto:elections@wvsos.gov). The reader-facing email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the West Virginia Secretary of State Elections Division, GoVoteWV and your County Clerk for official election information. These resources provide voter registration, registration lookup, polling-place information, early-voting information, absentee-ballot applications and tracking, voter identification requirements, accessibility information, military and overseas voting guidance, election calendars, candidate information and other voter services. West Virginia County Clerks administer voter registration, absentee voting, early voting and many local election operations.
official_resources.glance_value: Secretary of State, GoVoteWV & County Clerks
